title: Generation of vascularized human cardiac organoids for 3D in vitro modeling
protocol: Thaw growth factors before use.
Wash pluripotent stem cells with RPMI base media on Day 0.
Add differentiation medium containing BMP-4, Activin A, bFGF, and CHIR99021 immediately prior to use.
Warm differentiation medium to 37°C before adding it to the cells.
Prepare 5 mL of RPMI B27 minus insulin medium per T25 flask on Day 0.
Add IWP4 to the medium on Day 3 at a final concentration of 5 μM.
Wash cell with RPMI base medium on Day 3 to remove cell debris.
Warm RPMI base medium and IWP4 to 37°C before adding them to the cells.
Prepare 5 mL RPMI/B27 medium plus insulin per T25 flask on Day 6, 8, and 10.
Add 5 μM IWP4 to the prepared medium.
Perform a media change with RPMI/B27 plus insulin without factors on Day 13.
Harvest cells for organoid generation on Day 15 as outlined below.
Prepare PDMS culture plates from step 23 for use.
Ensure no residual ethanol remains in the well inserts inside a biosafety hood.
Coat inserts with 3% BSA in PBS (approximately 5–10 μL per well) for >60 minutes at room temperature (15°C-25°C).
Aspirate medium from T25 flasks.
Add 2.5 mL collagenase I per T25 and incubate for 1 hour at 37°C in 5% CO2.
Gently tap the side of the flask every 10 minutes to help dissociation.
Add 7.5 mL PBS (no calcium, no magnesium) to T25 flasks.
Titrate liquid and cells up and down approximately 5 times with a 10 mL serological pipette to disrupt cell clusters.
Collect cell solution into a 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the collected cell solution at 300 × g for 3 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant from the centrifuged cells.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 5 mL of 0.25% Trypsin with EDTA per T25 flask.
Gently agitate the resuspended cells in a water bath at 37°C for 10 minutes.
Aspirate 3% BSA from step 6b in the well inserts and ensure no residual liquid remains.
Centrifuge cell suspension for 300 × g for 3 min.
Filter cells through 100 μm Corning cell strainer.
Perform cell count.
Prepare organoid matrix mixture on ice using a P200 pipette tip.
Avoid introducing bubbles into the matrix mixture by slow pipetting and keeping the pipette tip under liquid surface.
Aliquot collagen I slowly into a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube as specified in the ‘Organoid Matrix Mixture’ table.
Add cold 10x DMEM to the collagen and mix thoroughly with the pipette tip as indicated in the table.
Mix 0.1 M NaOH with the mixture as specified in the ‘Organoid Matrix Mixture’ table.
Mix Matrigel™ thoroughly.
Add reagents in the order listed above, mixing thoroughly at each step.
Keep all reagents and Eppendorf tubes on ice constantly.
Aspirate supernatant from cardiomyocyte and stromal cell pellet.
Re-suspend cells in cold serum-free medium.
Add cardiomyocyte and stromal cell suspension to matrix mixture immediately.
Mix thoroughly with a P200 pipette tip.
Place PDMS culture plate on ice.
Seed mixture into each well of the PDMS culture insert throughout the entire seeding reservoir.
Tilt plate towards user and pipette mixture from bottom rows working up to ensure coldness before centrifugation.
Centrifuge plate at 100 × g for 10 seconds with maximum acceleration.
Transport plate to the centrifuge on ice.
Remove plate from centrifuge and check even cell spread under microscope.
Return plate to incubator and store for ∼30 min at 37°C 5% CO2 until mixture turns opaque.
Add 150 μl per well of Serum Free medium.
Aspirate medium on day 2 of organoid culture.
Add 150 μl Maturation Medium per well.
On day 5 of organoid culture, aspirate medium and add 150 μL MaturationMedium per well supplemented with 10 ng/mL PDGF-BB, 10 ng/mL FGF-2, and 33 μg/mL aprotinin.
On day 7 of organoid culture, aspirate medium and add 150 μL Weaning Medium per well.
On day 9 of organoid culture, aspirate medium and add 150 μL Weaning Medium per well.
On day 11 of organoid culture, aspirate medium and add 150 μL Weaning Medium per well.
Switch on microscope with 4x objective and CO2 and temperature control for force analysis of human cardiac organoids.
Wait for temperature and CO2 to stabilize before commencing imaging.
Focus Z axis on the top of the organoid pole using software control.
Set acquisition to record 500 frames over 10 s video (50 fps) with low magnification (4x).
Export multipage TIF files using naming system 001, 002 etc.
Use MATLAB script ‘TIF2AVI’ to batch convert TIF files into AVI video files.
Run ‘SettingConditions’ Matlab script to read first video.
Input ‘001.avi’ into line 3 within brackets in the script.
Select ROI by drawing a box around left-hand pillar.
Copy generated coordinates for the ROI into ‘poletracking’ Matlab script.
Aspirate culture medium from the plate containing organoids.
Add 50 μl of 1% PFA into each well and fix at room temperature for 60 minutes.
Gently remove the fixative from organoids.
Wash organoids twice with PBS.
Remove PBS gently.
Add 100 μL of blocking buffer to the sample for permeabilization at 4°C for 1–4 hours.
Prepare primary antibody stains by adding relevant antibodies to blocking buffer on ice.
Transfer 100 μL of blocking buffer to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Add primary antibodies such as Mouse IgG1 CD31 (1:400), Mouse IgG2A CD90 (1:500), and Rabbit cTnT (1:400) to the blocking buffer in the tube.
Aspirate the blocking buffer from organoids.
Add primary antibodies solution to organoids in the plate.
Incubate at 4°C on a rocker overnight (∼18 h) protected from evaporation using Parafilm and from light with aluminum foil.
Aspirate primary antibodies after incubation.
Add 100 μL of blocking buffer to organoids.
Place on rocker at 4°C for 1 hour.
Aspirate blocking buffer.
Add another 100 μL of blocking buffer to organoids.
Place on rocker at 4°C for 1 hour.
Prepare secondary antibodies by adding them to a new 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube containing 100 μL of blocking buffer on ice.
Transfer secondary antibodies such as Goat anti-mouse IgG1 Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400), Goat anti-mouse IgG2A 555 (1:400), and Hoechst33342 (1:1000) to the blocking buffer.
Protect from light.
Aspirate blocking buffer from organoids.
Add secondary antibodies to organoids in plate.
Incubate at 4°C on a rocker overnight (∼18 h) in the dark.
Aspirate secondary antibodies.
Add 100 μL of blocking buffer to organoids.
Place on rocker at 4°C for 1 h.
Aspirate blocking buffer.
Add 100 μL of blocking buffer to organoids.
Place on rocker at 4°C for 1 h.
Aspirate blocking buffer.
Prepare tissue clearing solution: 60% (v/v) glycerol and 2.5M fructose in PBS.
Add 50 μL clearing solution per well.
Image on fluorescence microscope with long working distance objectives, e.g., Leica Thunder Microscope using 4x and 10x objectives.
Prepare glass slide, coverslips and ProLongTM Glass Antifade Mountant.
Using end of pipette tip, wedge the organoids from poles and place on glass slide.
Add dropwise ProLongTM Glass Antifade Mountant on top of organoids.
Carefully place coverslip over sample and ensure no bubbles form.
Set overnight (∼18 h) at room temperature (15°C–25°C) before imaging.
Proceed to confocal microscope for fluorescence image acquisition.
Align replicate organoids with the same stain in a row on the slide for efficient imaging.
Pause point: Fixed samples can be stored protected from light at 4°C for 2 days.
